entities.text: Kondepu Hanumantha Rao vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Author: U. Durga Prasad Rao
Bench: U. Durga Prasad Rao
 Hon'Ble Sri Justice U. Durga Prasad Rao
 Criminal Petition No.5351 Of 2019
Order:

The petitioner/accused seeks to quash the proceedings against him in C.C.No.278 of 2019 on the file of Junior Civil Judge-cum- Judicial Magistrate of First Class, Mangalagiri, Guntur District, which was taken cognizance for the offences under Sections 188, 272, 273, 420 of IPC and Section 59(1) of Food Safety and Standards Act (for short, 'FSS Act').
2.

entities.text: Junior Civil Judge-cum- Judicial Magistrate of First Class, Mangalagiri, Guntur District
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
The allegations against the petitioner briefly are that on 01.09.2018 when the complainant along with his staff, on credible information rushed to the house of the accused near Veterinary Hospital of Tadepalli Municipality, searched the house of the accused, found banned tobacco products from his possession, seized the same, arrested the accused and registered a case in Crime No.336 of 2018 of Tadepalli Police Station, for the offences stated supra.
3. Learned counsel for petitioner while denying the FIR allegations would submit that even if the prosecution case is accepted to be true, tobacco products would not fall within the definition of Section 3(j) of FSS Act and therefore, the Police are not authorized to register the crime, investigate and file charge sheet and therefore, registration of the FIR is contrary to the provisions of FSS Act.
He relied upon the order of this Court in Crl.P.Nos.3731 of 2018 and batch, dated 27.08.2018.
As can be seen, in the said common order a learned Judge of this Court partly allowed the criminal petitions and quashed the offences punishable under Indian Penal Code and FSS Act.

4. So far as the offence under Section 188 of IPC is concerned, as per Section 195(1)(a)(i) of Cr.P.C,
no Court shall take cognizance of the said offence except on the complaint in writing of that Court or by such Officer of the Court as that Court may authorise in writing in this behalf, or of some other Court to which that Court is subordinate.
However, in the instant case, the F.I.R is registered suo moto basing on the report of the Inspector of Police of Tadepalli Police Station.
Therefore, it is the violation of Section 195 of Cr.P.C so far as the Section 188 of IPC is concerned and therefore, the said offence is also liable to be quashed.

5. Following the above order and for the reasons recorded therein, this criminal petition is allowed and the proceedings initiated against the petitioner/accused under Sections 188, 272, 273, 420 of IPC and Section 59(1) of FSS Act are hereby quashed.
